title: Yami Gautam Wins Best Actress at 72nd National Film Awards for Article 370
excerpt: The political action drama swept three National Awards including Best Feature Film and Best Music Direction, capping a remarkable 14-year career journey for Gautam.
body:
• Article 370 won three National Awards: Best Feature Film, Best Actress (Yami Gautam), and Best Music Direction for Songs (Shashwat Sachdev).
  • Kartik Aaryan and Mammootty shared the Best Actor honour for Chandu Champion and Bramayugam respectively, while Kalki 2898 AD won Best Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment.
  • Gautam dedicated the award to "dreamers everywhere," calling it the culmination of a 14-year journey in the film industry.

Three Awards for One Film

The 72nd National Film Awards, announced on Saturday, crowned Article 370 as the year's Best Feature Film — and handed its lead actress Yami Gautam the Best Actress honour for her portrayal of an intelligence officer navigating one of independent India's most consequential political decisions.

The film, which dramatises events surrounding the 2019 revocation of Jammu and Kashmir's special status under Article 370 of the Indian Constitution, also won Best Music Direction for Songs for composer Shashwat Sachdev. The triple win marks it as one of the most decorated Hindi films in this year's awards, adjudicated by a jury headed by filmmaker Jayaraj.

Directed by Aditya Suhas Jambhale and produced by Aditya Dhar's B62 Studios in collaboration with Jio Studios, Article 370 was praised by the jury for its storytelling and artistic merit. The film also features Priyamani, Skand Thakur, and Arun Govil in supporting roles.

"Every journey has a moment that reminds you why you never gave up. Today's that moment for me. This award is not the end of a dream. It is the beginning of a greater responsibility to keep growing, to keep taking risks, and to keep telling stories that matter."

— Yami Gautam

A Career 14 Years in the Making

For Gautam, the National Award represents the culmination of a journey that began in television before she transitioned to Bollywood. In an emotional social media post, she reflected on 14 years of work in the industry, describing the recognition as deeply personal. She dedicated the award to "dreamers everywhere," urging them to persist in their aspirations.

Gautam's performance in Article 370 was widely appreciated for its intensity and conviction. As an intelligence officer tasked with a high-stakes mission, she brought both physical rigour and emotional depth to a role that demanded she carry much of the film's narrative weight. Critics noted that the performance was a significant departure from her earlier romantic comedy roles, demonstrating a range that the National Award jury evidently recognised.

Aditya Dhar's Emotional Response

Aditya Dhar, who produced the film and is also Gautam's husband, expressed his elation in a heartfelt statement. "Winning three National Awards for Article 370 is a moment that is difficult to put into words," he said. "It is humbling, deeply emotional, and one that fills my heart with immense gratitude."

Dhar emphasised that awards were never the team's primary motivation. "We didn't set out to win awards. We set out to tell a story we believed in, with honesty and sincerity. To see that journey resonate with audiences across the country and now be recognised with the highest honour in Indian cinema is truly overwhelming."

He specifically acknowledged director Jambhale's vision and praised Gautam and Priyamani for their performances, while highlighting Sachdev's music as integral to the film's narrative impact.

Other Major Winners

The Best Actor honour was shared between Kartik Aaryan for his physically demanding role in Chandu Champion, where he portrayed athlete Murlikant Petkar, and Malayalam veteran Mammootty for his acclaimed turn in the period horror film Bramayugam. The shared win marks Kartik's first National Award.

Rajkumar Periasamy won Best Director for the Tamil military drama Amaran. The Telugu comedy Committee Kurrollu won Best Telugu Film, while Kalki 2898 AD — Nag Ashwin's ambitious sci-fi epic starring Prabhas and Deepika Padukone — was named Best Feature Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Sukumar's Pushpa 2 won Best Screenplay (Original), and Manoj Muntashir picked up Best Lyrics for Maidaan.

What the Win Means for Article 370's Legacy

The National Award validation elevates Article 370 from a commercially successful political thriller to a film with institutional recognition. For the Indian diaspora, many of whom closely followed the real-world events of August 2019, the film's success at India's highest cinematic honour underscores the enduring interest in stories that engage with contemporary political history.

Jyoti Deshpande, president of Jio Studios, described the moment as emotional. "I feel deeply grateful, humbled, and proud of every person who poured their heart into this film," he said. "We never began this journey with awards in mind."
